def: A type modeling the `std::ranges::range` concept: for an lvalue of it, `ranges::begin` yields an iterator and `ranges::end` yields a sentinel that forms a `sentinel_for` with it, both in amortized O(1) without modifying the range; when the iterator is a forward iterator, `begin` must also be equality-preserving.

The object corresponding to a subexpression E in [range.access]: if E is a glvalue, the object it refers to; otherwise the result of applying the temporary materialization conversion to E. All range access CPOs call `begin()`/`size()` etc. on an lvalue designating it.

A range modeling `std::ranges::view`: movable, declared via `enable_view`, with O(1) move construction, O(N+M) total cost for destroying N copies and M moved-from objects, and O(1) copying when copyable. The underlying range an adaptor holds by value is always a view.

A range that can be safely converted to a view by `views::all`: a view itself (constructible from the argument), a non-view lvalue, or a movable non-view rvalue that is not an `initializer_list`. All range adaptors require it for their first argument.

A range for which `ranges::begin` and `ranges::end` return the same type (`iterator_t<R>` and `sentinel_t<R>` are the same); C++17-style iterator-pair interfaces require it, and `views::common` can turn a view into one.
A range whose number of elements can be computed by `ranges::size` in amortized O(1), with a result equal to `ranges::distance(begin, end)`; a type can opt out by specializing `disable_sized_range`.
An input range whose elements cannot be modified through its iterators (the iterators are constant iterators). Introduced in C++23; `views::as_const` can convert any input range into one.

Exposition-only concept: view V and const V have the same iterator type and the same sentinel type. Adaptors pair `begin() requires (!simple-view<V>)` with `begin() const`, so that only the const implementation remains when the underlying view is simple.

A facility that transforms a range into a view with custom behavior (such as `views::filter`, `views::transform`), declared in `std::ranges::views`, which can be chained with `|` into lazily evaluated pipelines.

A customization point object that accepts a viewable_range as its first argument and returns a view; when it takes only one argument it is itself a closure object, and with multiple arguments, calling it with the arguments other than the range produces a closure object that binds those arguments by value (partial application).

A unary function object C accepting one range argument such that `C(R)` is equivalent to `R | C`; two closure objects compose as `C | D` into a new closure whose call pattern is `d(c(arg))`. Since C++23 user types can become closure objects via the CRTP base class `range_adaptor_closure`.

A facility that creates a view directly without taking an underlying range, such as `views::empty`, `views::single`, `views::iota`, `views::repeat`, `views::istream`; they are the sources of pipelines.

An exposition-only class template that behaves like `optional<T>`, except that default construction constructs a value, and when T is not assignable, assignment is emulated by "destroy and then reconstruct in place"; adaptors use it to store non-assignable function objects such as lambdas, keeping the view movable. Named copyable-box before C++23.

An exposition-only class template that behaves like `optional<T>`, except that copying/moving does not propagate the contained value (both the target and the moved-from source become empty); views use it to temporarily store iterators or prvalue inner ranges, so the cache belongs only to the current view object.

To meet the range concept's requirement that "begin is amortized O(1)", `filter_view`, `drop_view`, `drop_while_view`, `reverse_view`, `split_view`, `chunk_by_view`, etc. compute and cache the result on the first `begin()`; consequently they (usually) have no const `begin()`, and modifying the underlying range after caching yields stale results.

An empty class constructible from any arguments and supporting no operations; ranges algorithms that return iterators or subranges return it instead when the argument is a non-borrowed rvalue range, making the use of dangling iterators a compile error.

`std::generator<Ref, Val, Alloc>`: a coroutine return type that is also a move-only view modeling view and input_range; each `co_yield` produces one element, and `co_yield ranges::elements_of(r)` produces the elements of r one by one (nested generators recurse at O(1) per step).
